newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli stock market ends higher in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Israeli stock market ends higher in active trade.

text.p: Israeli shares rose on Wednesday for the sixth straight session in heavy trading despite expectations for a technical correction, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares gained 0.30 percent, or 0.69 points, to 229.84 on a heavy all-share turnover of 172 million shekels against 194 million shekels on Tuesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.46 percent higher at 238.20.
"The market continued to gain despite the fact that investors took profits. We were expecting a technical correction today but the market refuses to decline," a trader at Bank Hapoalim said.

"The provident funds continue to pour money into the market, but we need to see a correction. The market has been climbing too fast without any news to support the rise," added Eyal Kolka of Sigma Securities.
"Only a real change in the economy, including a reduction in interest rates and a devaluation of the shekel, will ensure that the positive momentum continues," Kolka said.
Other traders were more optimistic. "I believe that we will see a correction in the near future, but in the long run the market will continue to rise as new money comes in," the Hapoalim trader said.
Both traders ascribed the increase in activity since the start of the week both to the provident funds and to the mutual funds specialising in small-capitalization stocks.
Dead Sea Bromine rose 4.0 percent to 1,765 agorot after the company said on Wednesday that a senior delegation from Dow Chemicals Co is in Israel for talks.
Officials termed the visit very important but would not comment further. Newspaper reports said the two companies are discussing possible cooperation and exchange of know-how.
Israel Chemicals, Bromine's parent company and the most active share of the day, surged 4.75 percent to 314 agorot on turnover of 12 million shekels.
Teva Pharmaceutical Industries dropped 5.0 percent to 1,728 agorot. On Tuesday its Nasdaq-traded share fell 6.0 percent after Smith Barney downgraded the company to outperform from buy.

Other active shares included Koor Industries, which gained 0.5 percent to 30,484 agorot on turnover of 11.9 million shekels and Bank Leumi, which gained 2.25 percent to 501 agorot on volume of 6.6 million shekels.
